definition_en: A resource is an entry you add to the app that points to a place with your files, such as a folder on this device, a network folder, a cloud folder, a stream or a watch, and it appears as one item on the main screen.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'folder': a folder is a real directory that exists on a disk or server without the app, while a resource is the app's own saved entry that points to it.

definition_en: A folder is a place on a disk, memory card or server where files are kept, and it exists whether or not the app knows about it.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'resource': a resource is the app's saved entry that points to a folder. Use 'folder' only for the real directory itself, such as creating a new folder or picking one in the system folder window.

definition_en: A local folder is a folder stored on this device itself or on its memory card, as opposed to one on another computer or online.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'network folder' or 'cloud storage', which live on another machine or on the internet. The resource type list also shows local folders simply as 'Local'.

definition_en: A file is a single item stored in a folder, such as one photo, song, video or document.
disambiguation_en: Not always a 'media file': 'file' covers anything stored on a disk, while 'media file' means only the kinds of files the app can show or play.

definition_en: A media file is a file the app can show or play, such as a photo, GIF, video, audio track or document.
disambiguation_en: Not every 'file': other files in a folder, such as installers or archives, are not media files and stay hidden unless All Files mode is used.

definition_en: A virtual resource is a ready-made resource that gathers files of one kind from all over this device into one list, such as All Music or Camera Photos, without you picking a folder.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'folder': it has no single place on the disk.

definition_en: All Music is a virtual resource that lists every audio file found on this device, such as MP3 or FLAC tracks, in one place.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'playlist' and not the audio player: it is only the collection of local audio files, and it does not include network or cloud folders.

definition_en: All Videos is a virtual resource that lists every video file found on this device in one place.
disambiguation_en: Not the video player: All Videos is the collection you browse, while the video player is the screen that plays one video from it.

definition_en: All Images is a virtual resource that lists every picture found on this device, such as JPG, PNG, GIF or WebP files, in one place.
disambiguation_en: Not 'Camera Photos': Camera Photos holds only what the device camera took, while All Images includes every picture from every folder on the device.

definition_en: All Documents is a virtual resource that lists every document found on this device, such as PDF, EPUB, text and Office files, in one place.
disambiguation_en: Not the reader: All Documents is the list you browse, while the reader is the screen that opens one document. A text note created here is saved in the device's Documents folder.

definition_en: Camera Photos is a virtual resource that shows the photos and videos taken by this device's camera.
disambiguation_en: Not 'All Images': it holds only camera shots, not every picture on the device. A home-screen widget with the same name opens it.

definition_en: All Files is a ready-made resource that shows every kind of file on the device, not only media, and it works once All Files mode is allowed in Settings.
disambiguation_en: Not a virtual resource for one kind of media such as All Documents: All Files browses the device storage like a file manager, and how much it can reach depends on the storage access Android grants to your edition.

definition_en: Favorites is your own list of the files and channels you marked with a star (a heart on the watch), so you can open them again quickly from one place.
disambiguation_en: Not 'Quick Sort': marking a favorite does not copy or move anything, it only bookmarks the item. Spell it 'favorite', never the British 'favourite'.

definition_en: A destination is a resource you have marked for Quick Sort, so that one tap can copy or move the current file into it.
disambiguation_en: Not every resource: only resources marked for Quick Sort become destinations, up to 30 of them, each with its own number and color. In copy and move dialogs 'destination' also means simply the place a file is going to.

definition_en: A stream is a live internet radio, TV or video feed that the app plays from a web address instead of from a saved file.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'channel' in every sentence: the stream is the live feed or its web address, while the channel is the saved entry for it in the Streams list. Not 'Live Broadcast', which sends your own microphone or camera out to others.

definition_en: A channel is one saved radio, TV or video station in the Streams list, with its own name, logo and web address.
disambiguation_en: Not the 'stream' itself: the channel is the saved entry you pin, edit or remove, and the stream is what it plays. Not an audio channel such as the left and right sides of stereo sound.

definition_en: A playlist is a list of tracks or channels that play one after another, such as an M3U file you import into Streams or the Playlist gadget on the launcher desktop.
disambiguation_en: Not the 'queue' in the audio player, which is only the list of tracks lined up for the current session. Not a resource.

definition_en: The trash is a hidden folder named .trash where deleted local files wait, so you can still bring them back with Undo before the resource is closed.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'recycle bin' for the whole device: it works per resource and only where trash is supported, so on some network or cloud resources a deletion is permanent.

definition_en: A PIN is a code of 4 to 6 digits you can set on a resource so that nobody can open it without typing the code.
disambiguation_en: Not the lock-screen PIN of the device and not a 'pinned' channel or app: it protects one resource inside this app only.

definition_en: A text note is a plain text file you write in the app and save into the current folder or resource.
disambiguation_en: Not a Google Keep note: the app can send the text to Keep, but a text note is its own file in your folder. Not a voice note recorded on the watch.

definition_en: A scheduled operation is a file job, such as copying or moving files from one resource to another, that the app runs by itself on the schedule you set.
disambiguation_en: Not a one-time copy or move: it repeats on its schedule until you pause or delete it.

definition_en: A resource profile is a preset you pick for one resource, such as Audio Library, Video Library or Photo Storage, that tunes which files it shows and how it opens them.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'device profile', which tunes the whole app for a kind of device. The idea of a 'media library' is simply a resource with the Audio Library or Video Library profile.

definition_en: A device profile is a preset for the kind of device you use, such as a personal smartphone, a TV box, a car head unit or a photo frame, that sets sensible defaults for the whole app.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'resource profile', which affects one resource only.

definition_en: An app is any application installed on the Android device, such as a browser or a messenger, that the launcher can list and start.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'program': programs are the extra tools built into FastMediaSorter, such as Calculator, while apps are separate installed applications. The Russian and Ukrainian screens sometimes translate both with the same word.

definition_en: The main screen is the first screen of the app, where your resources are listed and where you add, open and manage them.
disambiguation_en: Not the Android 'home screen' and not the launcher 'desktop'.

definition_en: The file browser is the screen that opens when you open a resource and shows its files and subfolders so you can view, select, copy, move or delete them.
disambiguation_en: Never call it an 'explorer' or a 'file explorer'. A web 'browser' such as Chrome is a different thing, and qualified names such as 'video file browser' are allowed when the media type matters.

definition_en: The player is the full-screen screen that shows one file at a time, whether it is a photo, a GIF, a video or an audio track, and lets you move to the next or previous file.
disambiguation_en: Not only for video: 'player' is the shared name, and 'video player', 'audio player' and 'image viewer' name the same screen when it shows that kind of file. Documents open in the reader instead.

definition_en: The video player is the player screen when it plays a video, with controls for pausing, jumping forward or back and changing the sound.
disambiguation_en: Not All Videos, which is the collection you browse. 'Default video player' is the Android setting that lets the app open videos coming from other apps.

definition_en: The audio player is the player screen when it plays music or other audio, with the cover picture, the track controls and the queue.
disambiguation_en: Not 'Now Playing', which is the smaller view of the track already playing. Not All Music, which is the collection of audio files.

definition_en: The image viewer is the player screen when it shows a photo or picture, where you can zoom, rotate, crop or start a slideshow.
disambiguation_en: Not a separate app: it is the same player showing an image, and 'Default image viewer' is the Android setting that lets the app open pictures coming from other apps. Not All Images, which is the collection.

definition_en: The reader is the screen that opens documents and books, such as PDF, EPUB and text files, page by page.
disambiguation_en: Not the image viewer or the player. The Android default-app setting names the same role 'document viewer'.

definition_en: Now Playing is the view that shows the track playing right now, with its cover and controls, and leads back to the full audio player.
disambiguation_en: Not the audio player itself and not the queue, which lists what plays next. The same name is used by a launcher gadget, a watch complication and the 'Audio Now Playing' home-screen widget.

definition_en: Streams is the screen that lists your internet radio, TV and video channels, where you add, pin, edit and play them.
disambiguation_en: Not a single 'stream': 'Streams' with a capital S names the screen, while a stream is one live feed. Not 'Live Broadcast', which sends your own sound or picture out.

definition_en: Settings is the screen where you change how the app looks and behaves and switch optional programs and features on or off.
disambiguation_en: Not the Android system settings, which the app sometimes opens for permissions. The launcher has its own 'Launcher settings' and the reader its own 'Reader Settings'.

definition_en: A program is one of the extra tools built into FastMediaSorter, such as Calculator, Stopwatch, Network Monitor or the flashlights, that you switch on in Settings and open from the programs menu.
disambiguation_en: Not an 'app' installed separately on the device, and never a 'mini-program' or 'sub-program'. The watch lists its built-in programs under 'Apps', which is a known wording slip.

definition_en: The launcher is the part of FastMediaSorter that can replace the device's home screen with its own desktop, taskbar and app list, or show that desktop inside the app.
disambiguation_en: Not every 'launcher' on screen: in messages such as 'Your launcher does not support home-screen shortcuts' the word means whichever home-screen app the device uses. Turning launcher mode off brings back the previous home screen.

definition_en: The desktop is the launcher's main page, a grid where you place app icons, resources, channels, gadgets and sections, with separate layouts for the upright and the sideways screen.
disambiguation_en: Not the home screen of another launcher and not a computer desktop: it exists only while the FastMediaSorter launcher is in use.

definition_en: The home screen is the Android start screen you see after unlocking the device, run by whichever launcher app is set as home.
disambiguation_en: Not the app's 'main screen', and not the launcher 'desktop' unless FastMediaSorter is set as the home screen. Home-screen widgets and shortcuts are placed here.

definition_en: Calculator is a built-in program for everyday sums that you switch on in Settings and open from the programs menu, a widget or the watch.
disambiguation_en: Not the Android system calculator app: it stays inside FastMediaSorter.

definition_en: The camera is the app's built-in way to take photos and record videos and save them straight into a resource or folder you choose.
disambiguation_en: Not the Android camera app, and not 'Camera Photos', which is the virtual resource listing what the device camera took. 'Quick capture' is a widget that jumps straight into shooting.

definition_en: The drawing editor is the screen where you draw or write by hand on a photo, a screenshot or a blank page and save the result as a picture.
disambiguation_en: Not the crop or rotate tools of the image viewer. The menu item that opens it is simply called 'Drawing'.

definition_en: Screen recording is a program that records everything shown on the screen, with sound from the microphone, into a video file until you stop it.
disambiguation_en: Not a screenshot, which saves a single still picture. The programs menu labels it 'Screen video recording'.

definition_en: OCR (text recognition) reads the printed or written words in a photo or document page so you can copy, save or translate them.
disambiguation_en: Not translation by itself: OCR only finds the text, and translation is a separate step. 'Camera OCR' is the quick flow that does both from a new photo.

definition_en: Camera OCR is a program that takes a photo, finds the text in it and shows a translation next to the original words.
disambiguation_en: Not general OCR inside the player, which works on photos and documents you already have. The programs menu and Settings call it 'Camera OCR translation'.

definition_en: Network Monitor is a program that shows your connection, signal strength, addresses and speed so you can see why the network is slow or down.
disambiguation_en: Not a resource or a network folder: it only reports on the connection and opens no files.

definition_en: Immersive mode is the headset view that surrounds you with a 3D or 360-degree photo or video instead of showing it in a flat window.
disambiguation_en: Not full-screen mode on a phone. When immersive mode cannot start, the file plays in 'flat mode' instead.

definition_en: The resource list is the list of all your resources on the main screen, shown as rows or tiles.
disambiguation_en: Not the file list inside the file browser, which shows the files of one opened resource.

definition_en: A panel is a strip of buttons or items along one edge of a screen that can usually be collapsed or hidden.
disambiguation_en: Use the specific name when it matters, such as 'command panel', 'programs panel', 'streams panel', 'quick-access panel' or 'taskbar'. In the headset 'panel' also means the flat window that floats in front of you.

definition_en: The command panel is the set of buttons in the player for acting on the current file, such as copy, move and delete.
disambiguation_en: Not the three-dots menu and not Quick Sort alone. A setting decides whether it opens by itself when the player starts.

definition_en: The programs panel is an optional bar above the resource list on the main screen that gives one-tap access to your programs.
disambiguation_en: Not the 'quick-access panel' of the launcher. In Russian and Ukrainian the quick-access panel is also translated as 'panel of programs', which is a known clash.

definition_en: The streams panel is an optional bar above the resource list on the main screen that shows your pinned channels for one-tap playback.
disambiguation_en: Not the Streams screen, which lists all channels: only pinned channels appear on this panel.

definition_en: The quick-access panel is a pop-up panel of your chosen apps and shortcuts that you can open from the launcher or with a gesture at the screen edge.
disambiguation_en: Not the 'programs panel' on the main screen.

definition_en: The taskbar is the launcher's bar at the top or bottom of the screen with the Start button, pinned apps, recently used apps, the clock and status icons.
disambiguation_en: Not the Android status bar or navigation bar.

definition_en: A gadget is a small live block on the launcher desktop, such as a clock, weather, compass, battery or map, that shows fresh information and reacts to taps.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'widget': a widget is placed on the Android home screen of any launcher, while a gadget belongs to the FastMediaSorter desktop.

definition_en: A widget is a small live block from FastMediaSorter that you place on the Android home screen, such as Favorites, Random Photo Frame, Stopwatch or Scheduled Operations.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'gadget', which lives on the FastMediaSorter launcher desktop. Not a watch 'tile' or 'complication'.

definition_en: A section is a named group on the launcher desktop, such as Gadgets, Resources or Apps, that keeps related icons together under one heading.
disambiguation_en: Not a settings category and not a folder: a section only arranges desktop items and can be renamed, re-sorted or deleted.

definition_en: All apps is the launcher's full list of the apps installed on the device, opened from the launcher menu.
disambiguation_en: Not the programs menu, which lists FastMediaSorter's own programs. The Russian and Ukrainian screens translate it as 'all programs', which is a known clash.

definition_en: A badge is a small label drawn on top of a thumbnail or row, such as GIF, VR or Pinned, that tells you something about the item at a glance.
disambiguation_en: Not a button in general, although the VR badge can be tapped to try opening VR again. The word 'badge' itself never appears on screen, so describe what the badge says.

definition_en: Quick Sort is the feature that lets you copy or move the file you are viewing into one of your numbered destinations with a single tap.
disambiguation_en: Not 'Favorites', which only bookmarks a file.

definition_en: Grid view shows files, resources or channels as picture tiles arranged in rows and columns.
disambiguation_en: Not 'list view', which shows one item per line with more text. The file browser can be set to open in grid view by default.

definition_en: List view shows files, resources or channels one per line, with the name and details next to a small picture.
disambiguation_en: Not 'grid view', which shows larger picture tiles in rows and columns.

definition_en: A slideshow shows the files of a folder one after another by itself, moving to the next photo after the number of seconds you set.
disambiguation_en: Not a video made from photos: nothing is saved, it is only a way of viewing. Music can play in the background during a slideshow.

definition_en: Touch zones are invisible areas of the full-screen player, laid out as a grid of nine, where a tap does a set job such as next file, copy, move or delete.
disambiguation_en: Not visible buttons: the zones stay hidden unless you turn on the touch zones overlay or hint. With the grid switched off the player uses three simpler zones.

definition_en: The queue is the list of tracks lined up to play next in the audio player.
disambiguation_en: Not a saved 'playlist': the queue belongs to the current listening session only.

definition_en: The three-dots menu is the menu that opens from the button with three vertical dots and holds the less common actions for an item or a screen.
disambiguation_en: Some settings show the same menu as the symbol ⋮. It is not the programs menu.

definition_en: A shortcut is an icon you place on the home screen or the launcher desktop that opens one resource, channel, program or contact directly.
disambiguation_en: Not a widget, which shows live content, and not the item itself: removing a shortcut deletes nothing.

definition_en: The color theme sets the overall look of the app, such as light, dark or automatic.
disambiguation_en: Not the page theme of the reader (light, dark or sepia) and not the separate 'color scheme' of the watch. Always spell it 'color', never 'colour'.

definition_en: An edition is one of the separately published versions of FastMediaSorter, each made for a certain kind of device or store and with its own set of features.
disambiguation_en: Never call it a 'flavor' or 'build flavor' in user documentation. An edition is not a version number, which changes with every update.

definition_en: The Standard edition is the recommended full edition for phones, tablets, TVs and car head units.
disambiguation_en: Not the noLegal edition, which adds sideload-only extras on top of it. The Legacy edition covers older Android versions.

definition_en: The noLegal edition is a sideload-only edition, installed from an APK file outside the app stores, that adds what stores do not allow, such as the immersive VR player and full storage access.
disambiguation_en: Not the VR edition, which is the store-clean headset edition. The noLegal edition is never published in a store.

definition_en: The Lite edition is a lighter edition that plays local photos, videos and music only, without network folders, cloud storage, documents or Streams.
disambiguation_en: Not the Photos edition, which keeps network folders and cloud storage but drops video and audio.

definition_en: The Photos edition is an edition for pictures only, with network folders and cloud storage but without video, audio, documents or Streams.
disambiguation_en: Not the 'Photo frame' device profile, which is a setting inside any edition, and not 'Camera Photos', which is a virtual resource.

definition_en: The Legacy edition is an edition for older Android devices, starting from Android 6, with most Standard features but without the launcher and the watch companion.
disambiguation_en: Not an outdated or abandoned release: it is published together with the other editions.

definition_en: The VR edition is the edition published for VR headsets such as Meta Quest, with the full media set and immersive mode for 3D and 360-degree files.
disambiguation_en: Not the noLegal edition, which also runs on headsets but is sideload-only. The VR edition has no Chromecast and no watch companion.

definition_en: The FOSS edition is the open-source edition published in F-Droid, built without any closed-source parts, so it has no cloud storage, Streams, OCR, translation, Chromecast or watch companion.
disambiguation_en: Not a trial edition: it is complete within those limits. When writing about its open-source terms, spell 'license', never 'licence'.

definition_en: The phone is the Android phone or tablet that runs the main FastMediaSorter app and that the watch connects to.
disambiguation_en: Not only a phone in the strict sense: the same app also runs on tablets, TVs and car head units. On the watch, 'Phone' names the section with files taken from the phone.

definition_en: The watch is a Wear OS smartwatch paired with your phone, which can browse, play and record files with the FastMedia Wear app.
disambiguation_en: Not the software: the app on it is the 'watch app', and the phone-side program that controls it is 'Wear Companion'. A paired watch can also appear in the resource list as its own resource.

definition_en: The watch app is FastMedia Wear, the part of FastMediaSorter installed on the watch, where you browse and play files, streams and favorites right on your wrist.
disambiguation_en: Not 'Wear Companion', which runs on the phone.

definition_en: Wear Companion is the program on the phone that connects to your watch and decides which resources, streams and settings the phone shares with it.
disambiguation_en: Not the app on the watch, which is the 'watch app'. Not 'Fast Media Sorter for Windows', whose screens also say 'companion'.

definition_en: Wear OS is the system from Google that runs on smartwatches, and the FastMedia Wear app works only on watches that use it.
disambiguation_en: Not the watch app itself and not a brand of watch: it is the software platform, the way Android is for phones.

definition_en: A tile is a full-screen card on the watch that you reach by swiping from the watch face, showing a chosen resource, stream, your favorites or your programs for one-tap access.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'complication', which is a small spot on the watch face itself. Not the quick settings tiles on the phone, such as Live Broadcast.

definition_en: A complication is a small spot on the watch face that shows live information from the watch app, such as the last resource, the number of favorites or the track now playing, and opens it with a tap.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'tile', which is a whole screen you swipe to. The word comes from Wear OS and appears only in the watch face editor, never in the app's own screens.

definition_en: A VR headset is a device you wear on your head, such as Meta Quest, that shows 3D and 360-degree photos and videos all around you.
disambiguation_en: Not a phone-in-a-box viewer such as Google Cardboard, which only splits the phone screen in two. Immersive mode needs a real headset with the VR or noLegal edition.

definition_en: Meta Quest is a family of VR headsets made by Meta, such as Quest 3, on which the VR edition of the app runs.
disambiguation_en: Not the only supported headset: Android XR headsets work too, so say 'VR headset' when the brand does not matter.

definition_en: A TV is a television, an Android TV box or a media box that either runs the app with a remote control or shows what you cast to it.
disambiguation_en: Not 'Live TV', which is a category of channels in Streams. On a TV the app is operated with the D-pad of the remote instead of touch.

definition_en: The D-pad is the four-arrow pad with a center button on a TV remote, game controller or keyboard that moves the selection around the screen.
disambiguation_en: Not touch gestures: everything on screen can also be reached with the D-pad, which matters on TVs and in cars.

definition_en: A car head unit is the Android screen built into the dashboard of a car, where the app can play media with large, easy buttons.
disambiguation_en: Not a phone mounted in the car: it is the car's own Android screen, and the Car head unit device profile sets the app up for it.

definition_en: A network folder is a shared folder on another computer, a NAS or a router on your home or office network that the app opens over SMB.
disambiguation_en: Not a folder on this device and not cloud storage. People often say 'network share' or 'shared folder'.

definition_en: A network resource is a resource that points to a folder on another computer or server over the network, using SMB, FTP or SFTP.
disambiguation_en: Not a cloud resource, which lives with an online service such as Google Drive. Only network resources can be sent to the watch.

definition_en: SMB is the common way Windows PCs, NAS boxes and routers share folders over a home or office network, and the app uses it to open network folders.
disambiguation_en: Not FTP or SFTP, which reach a server by its address rather than a shared folder. Not a cloud service.

definition_en: FTP is an older, unencrypted way to reach folders on a server, still used by many routers and home servers.
disambiguation_en: Not 'SFTP', which is the encrypted and safer choice when the server supports it. The resource type list shows both together as 'SFTP / FTP'.

definition_en: SFTP is an encrypted way to reach folders on a server or computer by its address, a user name and a password or key.
disambiguation_en: Not 'FTP', which sends everything unencrypted. Fast Media Sorter for Windows also shares PC folders with the app over SFTP.

definition_en: Cloud storage is online space from a service such as Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox, where your files are kept on the internet instead of on a device.
disambiguation_en: Not a network folder on your own home network. A resource that points into cloud storage needs you to sign in to the service first.

definition_en: A cloud provider is the online service whose storage you connect to the app: Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox.
disambiguation_en: Not the storage itself: you pick a cloud provider, sign in, and then choose folders from its cloud storage.

definition_en: Google Drive is the cloud storage from Google, which the app can open as a resource after you sign in with your Google account.
disambiguation_en: Not only a place for resources: the app can also save a copy of its settings and resources to Google Drive. The Russian and Ukrainian screens write it as 'Google Диск'.

definition_en: Dropbox is a cloud storage service that the app can open as a resource after you sign in to your Dropbox account.
disambiguation_en: Not Google Drive or OneDrive: each service needs its own sign-in.

definition_en: OneDrive is the cloud storage from Microsoft, which the app can open as a resource after you sign in with a Microsoft account.
disambiguation_en: Not a network folder on a Windows PC: OneDrive files live on the internet, not on your local network.

definition_en: The catalog is the built-in list of internet radio and TV channels that the app downloads so you can add them to Streams without typing any web addresses.
disambiguation_en: Not your own channel list: channels you added by hand stay when the catalog is updated or cleared. Spell it 'catalog', never 'catalogue'.

definition_en: Live Broadcast is a program that sends what the microphone of your phone, and optionally its camera, picks up live over the local network so that other devices can listen or watch.
disambiguation_en: Not a 'stream' you receive: Live Broadcast sends your own sound or picture out. The Russian and Ukrainian screens name it with a different word from the one used for streams.

definition_en: Chromecast is the technology from Google for sending a video, photo or song from the app to a TV so it plays there instead of on the phone.
disambiguation_en: Not Live Broadcast, which sends your microphone or camera to other devices. Casting is missing from the VR and FOSS editions.

definition_en: Fast Media Sorter for Windows is a separate program for Windows PCs that shares chosen PC folders with the phone app in a couple of clicks, paired by scanning a QR code.
disambiguation_en: Not 'Wear Companion' for the watch, although both are called 'companion' on some screens. The folders it shares arrive in the app as SFTP resources.
